title: MHRC-Bench: A Multilingual Hardware Repository-Level Code Completion Benchmark
claim: The benchmark spans several coding paradigms, each task pairing in-file and cross-file context with a masked target to complete.
layout: 3 side-by-side columns, top-to-bottom, dashed boxes, green 'Complete the target' bar
description: Three parallel columns show benchmark examples for Chisel (generator-based DSL), Xilinx HLS, and SystemVerilog (RTL). Each column opens with a dashed header box holding a logo and language name. Below it sit a dashed 'Cross file context' box and an 'In file context' box, both filled with syntax-highlighted code snippets and '......' ellipses. A red <TARGET> marker shows the completion position. A green banner with a robot icon, labeled 'Complete the target', comes next. A dashed 'Ground truth' box follows it, holding the correct completion. Each column ends with its Code Structure type and Hardware Semantic type labels. The eye goes first to the language logos at the top and then to the green banners. The figure is dense with code and mostly black text, with purple keywords and red target tags.
caption: Overview of our hardware code completion benchmark across multiple hardware description paradigms. We present three representative examples from domain-specific language (DSL) (e.g., Chisel), HLS languages (e.g., Xilinx HLS), and Register-Transfer Level (RTL) design languages (SystemVerilog). For each example, both in-file and cross-file contexts are provided, with the completion target explicitly marked. Models are required to predict the correct completion given the provided contexts, where "\textless TARGET\textgreater" indicates the completion position. More examples are introduced in Appendix [ref].
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved strong performance on code completion in general-purpose programming languages, but existing repository-level benchmarks focus almost exclusively on software code and largely overlook hardware description languages (HDLs). We present \textbf{MHRC-Bench}, consisting of \textbf{MHRC-Bench-Train} and \textbf{MHRC-Bench-Eval}, the first benchmark for multilingual hardware code completion at the repository level with functional evaluation. MHRC-Bench covers three major hardware design coding styles and annotates each completion target with code-structure-level and hardware-oriented semantic labels derived from concrete syntax tree (CST) analysis. Post-training billion-scale code LLMs on MHRC-Bench-Train enables smaller open-weight models to outperform much larger general-purpose models under matched context windows. Beyond aggregate accuracy, our analysis surfaces four findings that distinguish hardware from software code completion: \emph{(i)}~performance varies sharply across HDLs, with high-level synthesis (HLS) easiest and VHDL hardest in most settings across functional pass rate, exact match (EM), and edit similarity (ES); \emph{(ii)}~hardware accuracy is non-monotonic in code-structure depth, in contrast with the monotonic depth--accuracy curve known for software; \emph{(iii)}~accuracy plateaus once the input context exceeds 2{,}048 tokens, while software completion continues to benefit from longer context; and \emph{(iv)}~certain repository-level retrievers tuned on software underperform a no-retrieval baseline on HDL repositories because their structural and dependency assumptions are violated by hardware code.
